title: Ministerial statement on no further action over COP findings on Sylvia Lim and Faisal Manap
what_it_is: A Ministerial Statement by the Leader of the House on the Committee of Privileges findings about Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, concluding that no further action need be taken by the House because the PPIPA time-bar prevents penalties.
why_it_matters: The statement says the 15th Parliament cannot impose penalties under the PPIPA for this conduct because it took place in the First Session of the 14th Parliament. The Leader of the House says no further action need be taken by the House in relation to the Committee's finding regarding Ms Lim and Mr Faisal. The record does not set out the practical impact.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House said one matter remained outstanding from the 14 January 2026 Motion: the implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

key_points.point: She said the Committee of Privileges found Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were untruthful to the COP about what was said at the 8 August meeting.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: the Committee's finding that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were untruthful to the COP about what was said at the 8 August meeting.

key_points.point: She said the Committee recommended deferring consideration of what, if anything, should be done about their conduct until investigations and/or criminal proceedings against Mr Singh concluded.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The Committee therefore recommended that consideration of what, if anything, should be done about their conduct of stating untruths to the Committee should be deferred until the conclusion of investigations and/or criminal proceedings against Mr Singh.

key_points.point: She said Parliament accepted the Committee's recommendation.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

key_points.point: She said the criminal proceedings against Mr Singh concluded on 4 December 2025 when the High Court Judgement was delivered.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The criminal proceedings against Mr Singh concluded on 4 December 2025 when the High Court Judgement was delivered.

key_points.point: She said the Courts' findings directly contradict Ms Lim's and Mr Faisal's evidence.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: The Courts' findings directly contradict Ms Lim's and Mr Faisal's evidence.

key_points.point: She said the relevant conduct took place in 2021 during the First Session of the 14th Parliament.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: the relevant conduct of Ms Lim and Mr Faisal took place in 2021, during the First Session of the 14th Parliament.

key_points.point: She said under section 22 of the PPIPA, it is no longer open to the 15th Parliament to impose any penalties for this conduct.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: it is no longer open to this 15th Parliament to impose any penalties in respect of this conduct under the PPIPA.

key_points.point: She said the House could pass a Motion to express regret, but in her view no further action need be taken by the House in relation to the Committee's finding regarding Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: it is my view that no further action need be taken by this House in relation to the Committee's finding regarding Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

key_points.point: She said that unless any Member objects, the matter can be brought to a close.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Unless any Member objects, we can now bring this matter to a close.

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim said she was not standing up to object to the Minister's proposal.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: I am not standing up to object to it.

key_points.point: Ms Indranee Rajah thanked Ms Lim for indicating she would not object and said her own statements from 14 January are on record.
key_points.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
key_points.quote: I thank Ms Lim for her indication that she will not be objecting to my recommendation.

key_points.point: The Speaker said that under Standing Order 23, Members may seek clarification on the Ministerial Statement but no debate shall be allowed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: pursuant to Standing Order 23, Members may seek clarification on the Ministerial Statement, but no debate shall be allowed thereon.

key_points.point: The Speaker declared the Ministerial Statement ended and called the Introduction of a Government Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: End of Ministerial Statement. Introduction of Government Bill.

what_happens_next: The Leader of the House said that unless any Member objects, the matter can be brought to a close. The Speaker then declared the Ministerial Statement ended and called the Introduction of a Government Bill.
not_said: Whether any Member will object to bringing the matter to a close.
What the terms of any Motion expressing regret would have been.
What specific evidence from the High Court judgment was considered in relation to Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.
What other steps, if any, the House could take in relation to the Committee's findings.
What the Government Bill introduced after the Ministerial Statement concerns.
